title: Gradient garter wrap
subtitle: A side-to-side asymmetric garter wrap in DK with a colour gradient.
excerpt: A side-to-side asymmetric wrap in DK wool, worked flat from a cast-on tip to a cast-off tip with increases on one long edge and a gradual colour change from one skein to another. Wingspan approximately 170 cm, depth approximately 40 cm. About 200 g of each of two DK yarns in related colours.
sourceNotes: Side-to-side asymmetric shawl construction is a contemporary form with no single period source. The gradual skein-to-skein gradient technique uses a standard Russian join for a smooth yarn transition.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 44 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Wingspan approximately 170 cm. Depth at deepest point approximately 40 cm. Blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A method of joining two yarn ends invisibly: the old and new ends are each threaded through their own plies using a tapestry needle, then looped through each other to form a secure join with no tails to weave in.

content.text: A side-to-side DK garter wrap fading from colour A to colour B across the wingspan. Worked from one short tip to the other with upper-edge increases. Approximately 170 cm wide and 40 cm deep.

The asymmetric side-to-side construction grows the wrap from one pointed tip to the other along the wingspan. Increases run along only the upper (back-neck) edge, so the lower edge stays straight. The colour gradient joins colour A and colour B at the midpoint of the wingspan using a
Russian join
for a clean transition. Budget about 200 g (440 m / 480 yards) of each colour.
What you need

items.name: Colour A
items.qty: About 200 g (440 m / 480 yards) of DK-weight yarn

items.name: Colour B
items.qty: About 200 g (440 m / 480 yards) of DK-weight yarn in a related colour

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular or straight needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked. If your blocked gauge reads 24 stitches per 10 cm, the wrap at the same stitch count will be approximately 156 cm rather than 170 cm. At a simple garter wrap this is a comfortable finishing point. Move to 4.5 mm needles if your swatch runs consistently tight.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast on

Using colour A and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 4 stitches. For the long-tail tail, allow approximately (4 × 4) / 10 + 15 = 16.6 cm. Knit 4 plain garter rows. On row 5 (RS), place a marker after stitch 2 to mark the upper-edge increase position.
Body
RS: k to marker, yo, SM, k to end. (1 stitch added on upper edge each RS row)
WS: k all sts.

Work in colour A for the first half of the wingspan (to approximately 215 RS increase rows, giving 4 + 215 = 219 sts, wingspan approximately 85 cm). Join colour B using the Russian join and continue in colour B for the second half. Continue until total wingspan reaches 170 cm.
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off across all stitches on a RS row. The total stitch count at cast-off is approximately 4 + 430 = 434 stitches at gauge.
Stitch count check-ins
After 100 RS rows: 4 + 100 = 104 stitches. Wingspan approximately 39 cm. The wrap shape is already visible.
At colour join (approximately 215 RS rows): 219 stitches. This is the halfway point. Check the Russian join is secure and the tails are woven in before continuing.
Common faults

Colour join visible as a bump: the Russian join was worked too loose, leaving a small loop between the two yarn ends. Work the join tightly; when the plies are threaded and looped, pull the join firmly before continuing.

Lower edge curling: garter stitch lies flat and should not curl. If the lower edge is rolling, the selvedge stitches are being slipped instead of knitted. Knit every selvedge stitch on both RS and WS rows.
Gradient line abrupt rather than gradual: introduce colour B by alternating one row of B with two rows of A over a 10-row band at the midpoint.
Blocking

Soak in cool water, press out in towels, pin to stated dimensions. Pin the lower straight edge in a straight line and the upper curved edge in a gentle arc. The gradient line should sit at the centre of the wingspan after pinning.
Care

Hand wash gently in cool water. Lay flat to dry. If the gradient colours were not pre-washed, wash the finished wrap with the colours face down on a white cloth for the first wash to check for dye bleed.
What to try next
A three-colour gradient, using colour A, a transition skein, and colour B in thirds, gives a more gradual fade across the full wingspan.
